title: A Drug Acts On One Step

scenes.tts: In membranes from cultured cells, the drug paroxetine fills half of the human serotonin transporters at only zero point zero eight nanomolar. Does that explain why some depressed people improve? It does not. To see why, look at what the drug acts on. A transmitter works as a system.
scenes.caption: In membranes from cultured cells, the drug paroxetine fills half of the human serotonin transporters at only 0.08 nM. Does that explain why some depressed people improve? It does not. To see why, look at what the drug acts on. A transmitter works as a system.
scenes.visual: A membrane bar with a row of transporter chips; purple paroxetine dots dock on half of them; an arrow leads to a boxed question mark: why do some depressed people improve?
scenes.narration: In membranes from cultured cells, the drug paroxetine fills half of the human serotonin transporters at only 0.08 nM. Does that explain why some depressed people improve? It does not. To see why, look at what the drug acts on. A transmitter works as a system.

scenes.tts: A transmitter system has three parts. The source is the set of neurons that make and release the chemical. The readers are the receptors. Some readers are ion channels, which act in about a millisecond. Others are G protein coupled receptors, which act in tens of milliseconds to seconds through messengers inside the cell. The off switch ends the signal.

scenes.visual: A synapse is built: terminal (source), yellow transmitter released across the cleft, two receptor types on the postsynaptic membrane with their speeds, then a transporter chip on the terminal labelled off switch.

scenes.tts: The off switch depends on the transmitter. Acetylcholine is broken down by an enzyme, acetylcholinesterase, at many synapses. Glutamate is cleared by transporters in glia and terminals. No enzyme in the cleft destroys it. Peptides are cut by peptidases. The amines, serotonin among them, are carried back into the terminal by transporters. The serotonin transporter is called S E R T.

scenes.visual: The synapse steps through four cases: acetylcholine dots vanish at an enzyme chip; glutamate dots enter transporters on terminal and glia; a peptide bar is cut by a peptidase; serotonin dots are carried into the terminal through the SERT chip.

scenes.tts: A drug changes one step. An agonist activates a reader. A competitive antagonist takes the reader's own site and prevents activation. A positive allosteric modulator binds a different site and strengthens the effect. An enzyme inhibitor slows the breakdown. A reuptake blocker occupies the transporter. Paroxetine sits in the central site of S E R T, where serotonin binds.

scenes.visual: The same synapse; a purple drug dot acts on a different step in each case: docks in the receptor's own site (response rises), takes that site (response stays at zero), docks in a second site (response grows), sits on the enzyme (dots stay), sits in the transporter (serotonin cannot enter).

scenes.tts: How much of the transporter does the drug fill? The fraction filled is L over K D plus L, where L is the free drug concentration. The dissociation constant, K D, is the concentration that fills half the sites. For paroxetine at human S E R T in cell membranes, K D is zero point zero eight nanomolar. At zero point seven two nanomolar, ninety percent are filled. The curve flattens at the top.
scenes.caption: How much of the transporter does the drug fill? The fraction filled is L over KD plus L, where L is the free drug concentration. The dissociation constant, KD, is the concentration that fills half the sites. For paroxetine at human SERT in cell membranes, KD is 0.08 nM. At 0.72 nM, 90% are filled. The curve flattens at the top.
scenes.visual: A curve of fraction filled against free drug concentration, computed from f = L / (KD + L); a point at 0.08 nM and 50%, then a point at 0.72 nM and 90%; the curve flattens.

scenes.tts: Filling the transporter is not a clinical effect. That these drugs block S E R T is established. That depression is caused by low serotonin is a separate claim. A twenty twenty two umbrella review found no consistent support for it. A twenty eighteen network meta analysis found all twenty one antidepressants it included more effective than placebo for acute major depression in adults, with certainty from moderate to very low. Both can be true. Aspirin relieves a headache, and headaches are not caused by a lack of aspirin. A drug's mechanism does not prove what causes the disease.
scenes.caption: Filling the transporter is not a clinical effect. That these drugs block SERT is established. That depression is caused by low serotonin is a separate claim. A 2022 umbrella review found no consistent support for it. A 2018 network meta-analysis found all 21 antidepressants it included more effective than placebo for acute major depression in adults, with certainty from moderate to very low. Both can be true. Aspirin relieves a headache, and headaches are not caused by a lack of aspirin. A drug's mechanism does not prove what causes the disease.
scenes.visual: Two linked boxes: established (drug blocks SERT) and a separate claim (low serotonin causes depression) joined by an arrow with a question mark; the two reviews beneath; then the aspirin and headache pair; the rule appears.
